title: Saint Thomas, Apostle
short_summary: Saint Thomas is one of the Twelve, remembered especially for his encounter with the risen Christ and his confession of Jesus as Lord and God.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps his feast on July 3.
John's Gospel calls him Thomas, also known as Didymus.
He confesses the risen Jesus as Lord and God.
Ancient tradition connects his later mission with the East and India.

sections.heading: One of the Twelve
sections.body: Thomas belongs to the apostolic foundation of the Church. The Gospels do not present him as a symbol only, but as one of the apostles chosen by Christ.

sections.heading: Faith before the risen Lord
sections.body: Thomas is often remembered for doubt, but the Gospel scene ends in confession. Before the risen Jesus, he acknowledges Christ in words of worship and faith.

sections.heading: Tradition of mission
sections.body: Ancient Christian tradition connects Thomas with missionary work eastward, especially toward India. The details should be handled with care, while the apostolic witness remains central.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Faith seeks Christ
catholic_connection_sections.body: Thomas shows that hesitant faith can be drawn by Christ into a clear confession of the risen Lord, not into a reduction of the Resurrection to an idea.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Apostolic witness
catholic_connection_sections.body: His feast keeps Catholics close to the apostles, whose witness grounds the Church's proclamation of the Resurrection.

historical_cautions: Traditions about Thomas's later missionary routes are ancient and important, but details vary across sources and should not be overstated.
